object: VirtualV LLM test suite as a whole (well-known suite, specialist suite, contamination audit, publication tooling)
assessor: self-assessment by the maintainers' agent; not reviewed by the BetterBench authors

criteria.criterion: Tested capability, characteristic, or concept is defined
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md §5 and §7 name the tasks per capability (arithmetic reasoning, code, knowledge, logic; specialist lanes), but give no formal definition of the capability each task stands for.

criteria.criterion: How tested capability or concept translates to benchmark task is described
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md §5 describes how each task is scored and combined into the composite; the link from capability to task is stated per task, not argued.

criteria.criterion: Domain experts are involved
criteria.evidence: Specialist packs are written in-house ('eigen holdout'); no external domain expert is named for any lane.

criteria.criterion: Domain literature is integrated
criteria.evidence: docs/PROFESSIONAL_SUITE_LESSONS.md and the dashboard's contamination section cite the literature (LiveBench, MMMU-Pro, lm-eval tasks); the specialist lanes cite one reference each.

criteria.criterion: Use cases or user personas are described
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md §1 and §11 describe scope and operator roles; README states the user (someone choosing a local model for given hardware). No explicit personas.

criteria.criterion: Differences to related benchmarks are explained
criteria.evidence: docs/PROFESSIONAL_SUITE_LESSONS.md compares against professional suites; the difference (hardware-aware, failures explicit) is in the README.

criteria.criterion: Input sensitivity is addressed
criteria.evidence: Contamination audit runs a paraphrased-MMLU lane and reports the paraphrase gap per model (scripts/benchmarks/contamination_audit.py; dashboard 'Parafrase-gap').

criteria.criterion: Has validated automatic evaluation
criteria.evidence: Scoring is deterministic and unit-tested (tests/test_eval_suite.py, HumanEval executes code), and the post-cutoff holdout key was corrected after a cross-model check; no separate validation study of the automatic scorers against human grading.

criteria.criterion: How benchmark score should or shouldn't be interpreted or used is described
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md §12 and the dashboard say a third-decimal difference is no ranking and give the interval; README says the numbers are not universal claims.

criteria.criterion: How knowing about the tested concept is helpful in the real world is described
criteria.evidence: README motivates the suite in one paragraph; no description of what a given score means for a real task.

criteria.criterion: Informed performance metric choice
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md §5 fixes the metrics and the unweighted composite and records why TruthfulQA is excluded from it; alternatives are not discussed.

criteria.criterion: Metric floors and ceilings are included
criteria.evidence: No metric floor or ceiling is published for any task.

criteria.criterion: Human performance level is included
criteria.evidence: No human performance level is included.

criteria.criterion: Random performance level is included
criteria.evidence: No random-guess level is included, although MMLU and BBH are multiple choice and the level is known.

criteria.criterion: Evaluation code is available
criteria.evidence: scripts/benchmarks/ is public under Apache-2.0.

criteria.criterion: Evaluation data or generation mechanism is accessible
criteria.evidence: Public tasks are fetched by scripts/benchmarks/bootstrap_public_data.py; the specialist and holdout packs are deliberately private, so that part is not accessible.

criteria.criterion: Evaluation of models via API is supported
criteria.evidence: --external-url plus the sanitising and CLI proxies; cloud rows for Claude, GPT-6, GLM and Gemini were measured this way.

criteria.criterion: Evaluation of local models is supported
criteria.evidence: llama.cpp and 1Cat-vLLM runners with hardware profiles.

criteria.criterion: Globally unique identifier or encryption of evaluation instances is added
criteria.evidence: The contamination audit has a canary-recall lane, but evaluation instances carry no GUID and the private packs are withheld rather than encrypted.

criteria.criterion: Task to identify if model has been trained on benchmark data is included
criteria.evidence: Canary-recall, paraphrase-gap and post-cutoff holdout lanes (contamination_audit.py).

criteria.criterion: Script to replicate results is explicitly included
criteria.evidence: scripts/reporting/build_release_evidence.py and validate_publication.py rebuild and check the published evidence; a single command that reproduces a published row end to end is not provided.

criteria.criterion: Statistical significance or uncertainty quantification of benchmark results is reported
criteria.evidence: scripts/benchmarks/score_confidence.py: Wilson intervals per component and a z-test against the leader, shown on the dashboard.

criteria.criterion: Need for warnings for sensitive/harmful content is assessed
criteria.evidence: No assessment of whether the tasks or model outputs need a content warning.

criteria.criterion: Build status is implemented
criteria.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push and PR; the README shows no build-status badge.

criteria.criterion: Release requirements are specified
criteria.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md and docs §10 state acceptance rules, and CHANGELOG.md plus tagged releases exist; a release checklist is in a maintainer's notes, not in the repository.

criteria.criterion: Requirements file available or equivalent is available
criteria.evidence: README names Python 3.12+ and lm-eval; there is no requirements file or pyproject.

criteria.criterion: Quick-start guide or demo is available
criteria.evidence: README 'Quick start' with a runnable example.

criteria.criterion: In-line code comments are used
criteria.evidence: Scripts carry rationale comments throughout (for example well_known_suite.py, result_store.py).

criteria.criterion: Code documentation is available
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md Appendix A is an operator manual; there is no per-module API reference.

criteria.criterion: Accompanying paper is accepted at peer-reviewed venue
criteria.evidence: No accompanying peer-reviewed paper.

criteria.criterion: Benchmark design process is documented
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md §9 and §10 document the process and change policy; the history of design decisions lives in commit messages and docs/MODEL_TEST_ROADMAP.md.

criteria.criterion: Test tasks & rationale are documented
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md §5 and §7 list the tasks; the rationale for the chosen samples (50/48/160/40 items) is not given.

criteria.criterion: Assumptions of normative properties are documented
criteria.evidence: The standard states that only matching protocol, engine and hardware are comparable; normative assumptions (what a 'good' model is) are not written down.

criteria.criterion: Limitations are documented
criteria.evidence: README and §12 state that results are not universal and that small differences are noise; the row-level evaluation_caveat field records known artefacts. No single limitations section.

criteria.criterion: Test environment design or prompt design process is documented
criteria.evidence: The prompt format is fixed by the protocol id (v4-mmlu-fewshot-20260918) and described in §5; how the prompts were designed is not documented.

criteria.criterion: Globally unique, persistent identifier for a dataset and its metadata is provided
criteria.evidence: Raw evidence is a checksummed GitHub release artefact; there is no DOI or other persistent dataset identifier.

criteria.criterion: Standardized metadata is included
criteria.evidence: No standardised metadata (for example Croissant) for the datasets or results.

criteria.criterion: Data sources and data collection process are explained
criteria.evidence: Public sources are named with their lm-eval task; the origin of the private specialist items is described only as in-house.

criteria.criterion: Data preprocessing steps are described (if applicable)
criteria.evidence: Sampling limits and the few-shot format are documented; the preprocessing of the private packs is not.

criteria.criterion: Data annotation process is described (if applicable)
criteria.evidence: Answer keys are in-house; one key was found wrong and corrected (CHANGELOG, contamination_audit.rescore_post_cutoff_holdout). No description of the annotation process.

criteria.criterion: Evaluation metric is documented
criteria.evidence: docs/VIRTUALV_LLM_TESTSUITE_STANDARD.md §5, §6 and §12 document every metric and the composite.

criteria.criterion: Applicable license is specified
criteria.evidence: LICENSE (Apache-2.0) and NOTICE.

criteria.criterion: Data representativeness is explained (if applicable)
criteria.evidence: No statement on how representative the 298 public items or the specialist items are.

criteria.criterion: Data is documented using a standardized format.
criteria.evidence: No datasheet or other standard documentation format for the data.

criteria.criterion: Code usability was checked within the last year
criteria.evidence: CI runs the suite's tests and validators on every push; last green run 2026-10-08.

criteria.criterion: Maintained feedback channel for users is available
criteria.evidence: GitHub issues and PRs are open and CONTRIBUTING.md routes disputes there; no stated response commitment.

criteria.criterion: Contact person is listed
criteria.evidence: .github/CODEOWNERS names the maintainer account; no contact address in the README.

zero_scores: Metric floors and ceilings are included
Need for warnings for sensitive/harmful content is assessed
Accompanying paper is accepted at peer-reviewed venue
Data is documented using a standardized format.
